findings.title: Unsubscribe does not mute users who are tracking or watching
findings.body: When a user's notification level is `tracking` or `watching`, this branch lowers it only to `regular`. Regular topics can still send notifications for replies and mentions, so the page's promise to stop notifications is not met. Set the level to `muted` for every unsubscribe request, regardless of the starting level.

findings.title: Saving the level directly lets auto-tracking undo the unsubscribe
findings.body: This direct save bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which stamps `notifications_changed_at` and sets `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed` when a notification level is explicitly changed. Email recipients can have a topic-user row with a nil reason; `update_last_read` treats that row as eligible for automatic tracking and can raise the level back to `tracking` after the user reads enough of the topic. Use the normal notification-level update path so the user's explicit preference is preserved.

findings.title: The GET unsubscribe endpoint changes user state
findings.body: This action is reached through a GET route but changes the current user's notification preference before returning the page. Because GET requests do not require a CSRF token, a cross-site link or navigation can trigger the change whenever the user has an active Discourse session. Keep GET read-only and require an explicit CSRF-protected action to apply the preference.

findings.title: The route name does not match the added template path
findings.body: This declares a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route, whose conventional template lookup is for `topic-unsubscribe`; the added template is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which corresponds to a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. There is no explicit template-name override, so visiting this route will not render the unsubscribe page. Nest the route under `topic` or provide a template matching the declared route name.
